 By SCOTT RICHEY

 Beat writer Scott Richey previews the Top 25 showdown between the Illini and Blue Devils at Cameron Indoor Stadium: 
 Beat writer Scott Richey’s storylines
 Round of flu-like symptoms
 Tomislav Ivisic scored a career-high 28 points despite playing just 22 minutes in Illinois’ 22-point win last Friday night against Sam Houston in Champaign.
 The 7-foot-1 center hadn’t practiced for two days prior to the Illini facing the Bearkats and was still dealing with the effects of an illness during the game. An illness that has made its way around Ubben Basketball Complex, hitting the team and coaching staff.
 “It’s gone through most of our team — all the sinus stuff and the coughing,” Illinois coach Brad Underwood said, adding Ethan Brown, Quentin Coleman and Andrej Stojakovic have all dealt with the same illness. “Just feeling all around kind of yucky and not very good. We’ve got a couple coaches with it. It’s just part of it this time of year. The main thing is we’ve got some of our guys in pretty good places health-wise now.”
 Mirkovic’s return still unclear
 David Mirkovic will not play Tuesday night at Duke. The 6-foot-9 sophomore forward — a preseason All-American — remains sidelined indefinitely after offseason foot surgery. Mirkovic, who is back out of the protective boot he has worn on his surgically-repaired left foot, did some shooting Monday ahead of Illinois’ practice.
 While he’s not practicing, he’s been able to return to the weight room following his appendectomy earlier this month.
 “Every day is a step closer to him being back in uniform,” Underwood said. “The one thing we’ve all got to understand is we’re 14-15 weeks removed from a lot of physical activity. The appendix set him back in the weight room. We’re not going to bring him back until he’s close to 100 percent and until he’s practicing with our guys and there’s some comfort out there. It’s step by step. ”
 Could get crazy at Cameron
 Underwood left Lubbock, Texas, last week impressed with the home-court advantage Texas Tech created at United Supermarkets Arena. The Illinois coach called the atmosphere “electric” and the Red Raiders’ fans “rude and crude.” Exactly what he wanted his team to experience in the second week of the season. Week three should offer more of the same with a trip to Durham, N.C., and an introduction to the “Cameron Crazies.”
 “Texas Tech is up there — definitely,” Ivisic said about the top road game environments he’s experienced. “Michigan State. Purdue last year was very loud. I would also say Nebraka my first year. But if I had to pick one, I think it would be Texas Tech. That was a good atmosphere and a good experience for the team and will definitely help a lot for the Duke game. But it’s also going to be a different type of environment. We’ve got to be ready for it.”
 The News-Gazette’s pick
 No. 5 Duke 92, No. 10 Illinois 87 
 Even not at full strength, Illinois proved it can go on the road, in a hostile environment, and compete with a Top 25 team. Eventually. Last Tuesday night’s loss at Texas Tech required a major second-half comeback attempt. Duke is a younger, albeit no less talented opponent. The Illini won’t be at full strength again — no Mirkovic and no Jake Davis — and that could prove to be a bigger issue against arguably the deepest team they’ll face all season. The Blue Devils are barely playing five-star freshman Cameron Williams, and he’s a projected first-round NBA draft pick. (News-Gazette prediction record: 3-1)

 ➜ FYI: Stojakovic is the second-leading scorer in the Big Ten through the first two weeks of the season, trailing only Southern Cal sophomore guard Alijah Arenas, who is averaging 22.8 points after dropping an impressive 21 points in 17 minutes on Arkansas-Pine Bluff on Sunday night. Stojakovic has topped 20 points in three of four games, with his 26 points against Sam Houston in the Illini’s 108-86 victory last Friday night at State Farm Center his season-best game.

 ➜ FYI: Blackwell has had an uneven first season for Duke, including a pair of games with just three points (Army and SIU Edwardsville) where he shot a combined 15 percent from the field. His season-high 17 points in the Blue Devils’ Champions Classic loss to Michigan State came on 6 of 16 shooting. In six career games against Illinois during his time at Wisconsin, the son of former Illini guard Glynn Blackwell averaged 14.7 points on 46 percent shooting, including a 35 percent mark from three-point range.

 Details
 ➜ Site: Cameron Indoor Stadium (9,314); Durham, N.C.
 ➜ Radio: Brian Barnhart (play-by-play) and former Illini Deon Thomas (analysis) will have the call on the Illini Sports Network on WDWS 1400-AM, WDWS 93.9 FM, WHMS 97.5-FM, WPXN 104.9-FM, WDAN 1490-AM, WDNL 102.1-FM, WSOY 1340-AM and WSOY 103.3-FM.
 ➜ TV: Kevin Brown (play-by-play) and Sean Farnham (analyst) will have the call on ESPN.
 ➜ Series: Duke leads 6-3.
 ➜ Last meeting: Duke won 110-67 on Feb. 22, 2025, at Madison Square Garden in New York. Illinois shot 8 percent from three-point range and suffered its biggest loss (by 43 points) in program history.
 ➜ FYI: Two of Illinois’ three wins in the series have come at Cameron Indoor Stadium. That includes an 83-68 victory on Dec. 8, 2020, with the arena empty because of COVID-19 protocols and a 75-65 win on Dec. 2, 1995, that snapped Duke’s 95-game nonconference home winning streak. Kiwane Garris scored 18 points off the bench to lead the Illini, while Richard Keene and Bryant Notree had 14 points apiece and Jarrod Gee chipped in 13.
 Scott Richey covers college basketball for The News-Gazette. His email is srichey@news-gazette.com , and you can follow him on Twitter ( @srrichey ).
